steps.text: Rinse and drain the quinoa. Bring water and quinoa to a boil in a saucepan over high heat, stirring occasionally. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes. Remove from the heat.
Blend together the milk, bananas, sugar, and salt in the bowl of a blender or food processor until smooth. Pour the milk mixture into the saucepan with the quinoa.
Place the pan over medium heat. Cook and stir until the mixture becomes thick and creamy, 5 to 10 minutes. Remove from the heat. Stir in the butter and vanilla and serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Quinoa Pudding
raw_recipe.description: High in protein, iron, vitamins, and minerals, quinoa is a supergrain (actually a seed) that is gaining popularity and can easily take the place of rice in many common recipes. This quinoa pudding is made with bananas, milk, and vanilla. It is a great basic pudding recipe to take in whatever direction you choose.

review.reviewBody: I really enjoyed this! I modified it by using vanilla almond milk so I did not add any more vanilla or sugar. About half way through I added dried cranberries and chopped walnuts. A fabulous and healthy desert!

I thought it was good. Next time I'll use Thai canned coconut milk. I would also like to substitute the bananas with something that won't impact the coconut flavor. I'll see what I can come up with. Suggestions are welcome.

I love this! I cooked the quinoa in milk instead of in water to make the pudding a little richer, and I used just 1 tbsp of sugar. I also skipped the butter, but it tastes great and thickened beautifully. Next time, I might add raisins and/or cinnamon, but I'm definitely making this again.

Have to say that I was a bit skeptical trying this..but I gave it a try…and was quite impressed. I only had one very ripe banana, used 2% milk, brown sugar and added Craisins. Skipped the butter and vanilla at the end as it really did not need it. It did thicken up a tad when cooked for a full 10 mins but is on the thinner side. I would think if you want it a bit thicker, try decreasing the amount of milk added. This recipe is a good base to start with and add varied flavorings and add ins to your taste or for what you have on hand. I did soak the quinoa for 15 mins and gave a good rinse until clear…does make a difference. Great as left overs too. Awesome. Thanks for sharing Lynda Q.

I loved this as a healthy dessert. I toasted the quinoa first, then added the water a little at a time, just covering the quinoa then letting it cook down, then covering again. This gives it a creamy nutty flavor. I used honey instead of sugar, it worked great. I am adding cranberries and walnuts to it tomorrow. Can't wait to try it that way, too!

I made this as written, with the exception of adding only 1 3/4 cup of milk (based on reviews saying they needed to thicken it further). As written, this has a mild banana flavour with a hint of vanilla and the consistency of soup. Very underwhelming. I have made many quinoa pudding recipes and this was by far the most bland, flavourless and runny. I actually can’t imagine that it would “thicken” at all looking at the ingredients, without simmering for an extended period to reduce it.

Per other reviews, I added a whole beaten egg, 1 tsp of cinnamon and 1/8 tsp of nutmeg, just to make it edible. I probably could have added an additional egg, (& another banana) but here during covid quarantine, I did not have one. Could still use more tweaking, even after the changes. I would not recommend this as written.

I read the lowest rated reviews and some higher ones. The recipe doesn't specify that YOU SHOULD COOK THE QUINOA UNTIL THICKENED before adding blended mixture, this doesn't necessarily happen in 15 minutes! This is a slow cook prep, but IT WILL THICKEN. 

Think of it as preparing oatmeal, add whatever makes you happy (but it doesn't taste like "dessert"!! I added dried cherries, ORANGE EXTRACT WAS AMAZING (maybe prepare quinoa with a juice instead of water as someone else suggested), cinnamon, nutmeg, allspice, xylitol (sweetner), and shaved sugared almonds. 

I think next time I will use a bit of brown sugar or maple!

Very tasty! I added in an extra bannana. After it had cooked for 10 mins. I put it back in the blender and pureed it. I then put it in a container and in the frig. This morning I scooped some out into a bowl, added a little bit of milk and microwaved it for a 1.5 mins. It was wonderful! More the texture of a creamy smooth cream of wheat. I also used skim milk for the recipe and the addition before reheating.

Making it right now actually! I subbed the white sugar with maple syrup and the butter with ghee. I also used 3/4 of the milk and 1/4 coconut milk which adds a nice background flavor. Color me impressed!

Actually I'd give this 4.5 stars. I used red quinoa, maple syrup instead of sugar and skim milk. It didn't want to thicken up for me though, so I added an egg yolk after 20 minutes of simmering then brought to a boil for 3 minutes. That did the trick. Stirred in vanilla and raisins. Delicious! Thank you so much for the great idea!

My son practically lived off of this when he was 9-12 months old and still loves it at 2 years. The only change I suggest is to add the milk on its own instead of putting it with the bananas in the food processor. It really helps reduce the foaming. It's a great healthy snack for little ones and big ones - on special days, put a dollop of Nutella on top. ;)
First attempt at cooking quinoa and found this recipe. So I added the currents as spoken about earlier and added strawberries and yogurt. Really great recipe

I made this tonight. I added cinnamon. And I had whipping cream that needed to be used so I added that and topped it off with 2% milk. It is super creamy. Oh, and I used 4 packets of Splenda instead of sugar. Plenty sweet!
No changes, yes I would make again.
I'm not sure I cared for the texture. For some reason when quinoa is cooked in milk it makes it like little pebbles. The taste of the banana was ok. My 11 year old like it.

I made this recipe dairy free due to recent food allergy testing, but it still came out nicely. If your banana is super ripe, I would add sugar (or maple syrup like I did) to taste. It does have a little bit of a banana taste to it, so if someone in your household doesn't like them I'd probably not include it. I used a combination of vanilla unsweetened oat milk and coconut creamer, and coconut oil to top it off. Actually my first time making quinoa and I'm pretty happy with it!
Just delicious.

I really liked this and, unfortunately, I had to make two changes. I started making it and realized I only had almond milk instead of regular milk. Also, I like raisins in my rice pudding so why not?

I would suggest you give this recipe a try.
Soooo yummy! I have been full all morning

I was looking for a basic quinoa pudding recipe to switch out my mom favorite rice and raisins recipe. I added cinnamon nutmeg cardamon raisins and a little brown sugar. Used almond milk instead of regular milk; Want to try with coconut milk.
